observation.body:
## Problem

Allow independent change-harness runs to progress concurrently without weakening any existing correctness, independent verification, recovery or publication guarantees. Quality takes priority over elapsed time. Shared resources may serialize; **unattended operation, durable waiting and automatic resumption are required**. Ordinary contention must not become a failed run, an approval question or an abandoned task.

This request arose when implementation of https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/10 could not start because https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/39 already occupied the harness's one active slot. This issue requests an implementation of safe concurrent runs; the research below is design input, not proof that such support exists today.

## What is actually shared today

Source reviewed at [`796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf`](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/tree/796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf), the target `master` revision during research on 28 October 2026.

- [`harness_state.py`](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf/.agents/skills/implement-change-harness/scripts/harness_state.py): `repository_lock()` uses a short-lived, nonblocking POSIX `flock` under the common Git directory. This is a local mutex, not a remote lease or a lock held throughout test execution.
- The same helper stores one `active.json` in one orphan `harness-artifacts` branch. `initialize` rejects another active root/run; `validate_run_records` treats another unfinished run as invalid. This **logical singleton is persisted remotely** and follows clones to other machines.
- Checkpoints use expected-old local ref updates and normal non-force remote pushes. `artifact_sync` requires exact-tip confirmation and preserves competing histories. `remote_history` deliberately refuses adoption of changed run-state bytes. Those protections detect competing writers; they do not schedule independent writers or combine concurrent state changes.
- Different machines ordinarily eliminate conflicts over local Steam installations, local files and local GPUs. They still share GitHub task identity, PR operations and the remote artifact namespace. Shared mounts, remote test services or the same Steam/account data can also cross machine boundaries. Separate machines therefore need independent run records even when no hardware mutex is shared.
- Worktrees help with source isolation; they do not give each run a private repository configuration, shared refs, operating-system environment or physical device.

Removing the single-active assertion alone, using another clone, or giving each run a differently named local lock is insufficient.

## Research: interference classes and mitigations

### 1. Git state, artifacts, task identity and integration

[Git worktree documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree) describes private HEAD/index state alongside shared refs and default configuration; it also cautions about incomplete submodule support. Give each run/worker its own checkout, branch or detached candidate, build tree, scratch space and output namespace. Avoid concurrent writes to shared Git config, common dependency checkouts or a mutable installed harness package; pin the helper/schema and tool identities for each run.

Independent machines still contend on the current artifact ref. [Git ref updates](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-ref) support expected-old checks locally; [normal push rules](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push) reject divergent updates. Neither is a distributed execution mutex. Options worth evaluating:

- Per-run orphan artifact refs, each with one canonical owner and exact-tip publication, plus a narrowly coordinated discovery/task-claim index. Use a ref namespace compatible with the existing `harness-artifacts` ref (a ref cannot also be a directory prefix).
- A single publication service that serializes short, validated transactions for multiple explicitly addressed runs in the existing branch.
- A transaction protocol that safely rebases **disjoint** run updates after rereading canonical state, without replaying external effects or merging conflicting state blindly.

Prefer the simplest design that meets the tests. Do not implement an automatic Git merge of arbitrary state JSON. Specify crash recovery, historical discovery, migration, owner takeover and exact publication semantics for the chosen layout. Global history validation must not be weakened to make contention disappear.

Claim the same canonical issue/deliverable at the correct repository-wide scope, including cross-machine starts and overlapping root/sub-issue runs. Different issues may run concurrently; two owners must not independently publish competing implementations of the same deliverable. Native dependency requirements remain authoritative. Material issue edits or target-base advances still invalidate affected approval tuples. Coordinate merge/wrap-up and branch cleanup with https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/39; a completed run must not clear another run's active entry, approvals or queued work. No merge authorization is implied by this issue.

### 2. Fixed names, writable files, caches and test schedulers

[`fossilize_test.cpp`](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf/test/fossilize_test.cpp) creates/deletes fixed relative filenames such as `.__test_tmp.foz`. [`test/CMakeLists.txt`](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf/test/CMakeLists.txt) supplies build-relative layer output; [`layer_test.cpp`](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf/test/layer_test.cpp) removes a dump-prefix glob. Different worktrees are insufficient if workers reuse a build/test directory. Use run/attempt-specific writable roots and immutable copied/read-only fixtures; resolve symlinks/aliases when identifying a shared resource. Cleanup must be restricted to owned paths, never broad user/global caches.

CTest offers [`RESOURCE_LOCK`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_test/RESOURCE_LOCK.html), [`RUN_SERIAL`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_test/RUN_SERIAL.html) and [resource allocation](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/ctest.1.html#resource-allocation). These are useful within a CTest scheduler. **Design inference:** independently launched CTest processes need an additional shared authority; their in-memory schedules are not a host-wide lock. Resource allocation is not activated merely by declaring `RESOURCE_GROUPS`: it needs a resource specification and test-side selection. Missing prerequisites or missing allocation must never be counted as a passing required gate.

[The Mesa environment reference](https://docs.mesa3d.org/envvars.html) documents explicit shader-cache placement and XDG/home defaults. Give cache experiments private, proven cache locations for the actual driver/runtime, preserving the intended cold/warm sequence. Do not disable caching as a concurrency workaround when cache reuse is what the test verifies. Do not assume an OpenGL cache setting isolates every Vulkan/Steam/vendor cache.

### 3. Steam, game sessions and physical GPUs

The existing [verification guide](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf/local-docs/verification.md) already requires baseline/candidate/restored-cache/warm-repeat phases, actual executable provenance, client/replay shutdown, original preservation and rollback. It warns against heavy device stress alongside a game. [`validate_roundtrip_sandbox.sh`](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/796bba75ab32c13e1b50ee01fd7d067f17112cdf/cli/validate_roundtrip_sandbox.sh) deletes home-level driver caches and fixed `/tmp/gears.*.foz`; it must not become an unattended concurrent test unchanged.

Treat a real Steam experiment as an **exclusive transaction across setup, all comparison phases, descendants, restoration and rollback verification**, not just a lock around launching `steam`. Canonical resource identity should include the host/installation/account/library or prefix actually touched, plus the relevant physical GPU. Different AppIDs are not evidence of isolation. A private output directory does not isolate client restart, launch settings, installed executable replacement, driver cache priming, user session, saved games or shared service state.

[Valve describes the Steam Runtime](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-runtime) primarily as a compatibility environment, including namespace-based containers. That is not a documented guarantee of independent Steam clients, cache state or GPUs. Do not claim containers or private HOME variables prove Steam isolation. Separate test users/VMs/hosts may provide stronger boundaries, but shared physical hardware or account/library state must still be inventoried and verified.

Conservatively serialize real GPU/cache tests on the same device until concurrency is specifically supported. Performance, timeout-sensitive and cold/warm comparisons need an appropriate quiet reservation against competing CPU/I/O/GPU work, not merely separate file paths. Device-reset/hang injection can require host-level exclusivity or a dedicated worker machine. Never launch destructive fault experiments on a normal shared desktop simply because other harness workers obey a mutex.

### 4. Locks, process lifetime and abandoned work

[Linux `flock`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html) is generally advisory: all participating launchers must cooperate. Lock descriptors refer to open file descriptions and can be shared across fork/dup; release behavior must be intentional. A lock inside a repository cannot coordinate another clone testing the same host resource. Use a stable host-wide authority for host resources and repository-wide authority for remote/task effects. Never unlink a live lock file or reclaim solely because a PID disappeared or a lease clock expired.

[Distributed-lock analysis](https://martin.kleppmann.com/2016/02/08/how-to-do-distributed-locking.html) explains how an expired lease owner can resume and write stale data. Use ownership generations/fencing at services that can validate them. Steam and a physical GPU cannot generally reject an arbitrary stale client's token: retain/quarantine their reservation until the old execution is confirmed stopped and restoration is established. Heartbeats and timestamps alone do not prove that.

The process completing a test can spawn grandchildren, daemonize or delegate to an existing service. Terminating only the shell is insufficient. [systemd process lifecycle controls](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.kill.html), [cgroup-v2](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html) and, on Windows, [Job Objects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects) offer process-group containment; delegation/breakaway and externally launched Steam services still need handling. Releasing a reservation requires verified quiescence of owned work, not killing unrelated user processes. Declare unsupported platforms honestly rather than silently substituting weaker behavior.

### 5. Resource pressure, hidden effects and the guarantee boundary

[Linux namespaces](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/namespaces.7.html) isolate selected resource classes; they do not promise exclusive physical GPU, memory bandwidth or storage capacity. [Bazel's sandbox documentation](https://bazel.build/docs/sandboxing) illustrates enforcing writable boundaries, optional network isolation and daemon cleanup, and explicitly selecting an isolation strategy instead of silently degrading. These are design patterns, not a requirement to adopt Bazel or privileged containers.

Use explicit CPU/memory/disk/process budgets and bounded build parallelism; cgroups can enforce several limits but do not establish performance equivalence or GPU isolation. Admission control should wait rather than provoke host OOM, disk exhaustion or spurious timeouts. A quiet benchmark/timeout reservation must conflict with ordinary heavy builds too. Record contention/pressure and invalidate contaminated evidence; a later successful retry must not erase a real failure.

No generic analysis can establish non-interference for arbitrary shell programs with unrestricted access. The supportable contract is controlled execution with declared resources, enforced writable/process boundaries, reviewed adapters for external systems and conservative serialization for unknown effects. Detection/tracing can reveal missing declarations; absence of a conflict in one run is not a proof. A host-exclusive lock excludes cooperative harness activity, not an unrelated human, desktop compositor or remote client. If those affect the assertion, establish dedicated isolation or leave the gate waiting/incomplete with an accurate reason.

### 6. Unattended waiting and orchestration

A mutex is a safety primitive, not a fair queue, restart mechanism or scheduler. Require a durable `waiting_for_resource` state with the requested set, owner, reason, queue order and resumption operation. Acquire complete resource sets atomically or in a documented total order to avoid deadlock; include hierarchical conflicts (host-exclusive versus GPU/CPU jobs) and prevent starvation. Do not hold an artifact transaction lock while waiting for hours of Steam access. Waiting runs must be able to checkpoint/cancel/recover without disturbing the owner.

A supported runner/supervisor must own waiting and automatic resumption across coordinator restart. An AI final response saying “retry later” does not meet unattended operation. Use bounded individual waits, durable retries/backoff and useful status; no busy loops, silent queue drops or repeated human confirmations for ordinary contention. Track queue time separately from actual command/repair budgets. Explicitly define deadline accounting so contention neither silently grants more execution/repair budget nor exhausts an unchanged four-hour run deadline into routine manual intervention.

[GitHub Actions concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) is a useful warning: cancellation and queue limits are policy choices, and groups apply within their documented repository scope. Current docs describe default replacement of a pending run and opt-in larger queues. An Actions group alone does not protect a locally launched test or another repository using the same host; any adopted scheduler must share the actual resource authority. Existing approval requirements for production actions remain; resource queueing adds no new approval step.

## Required outcome and acceptance criteria

1. **Concurrent identity and durable state:** At least two distinct ready issues can initialize, plan, implement, independently check and publish their own PRs concurrently, on one host in isolated worktrees and from separate clones simulating separate hosts. Every operation explicitly selects its run. Same-issue or overlapping-deliverable claims admit one owner and offer unattended observation/resumption rather than duplicate PRs. A run's completion, cleanup or migration cannot erase or modify another's state.
2. **Artifact correctness across machines:** Implement and document the chosen publication model. Preserve exact publication confirmation, immutable reports/history, privacy/destination binding, non-force source/artifact safety, uncertain-write recovery, stale-worker fences and all existing rejection guarantees. A normal update in run A must not strand run B in manual divergent-history reconciliation. Genuine same-run conflicts remain visible and fenced. Preserve schema1/2/3 history and live/saved run identity, acceptance and budgets during a supported migration; do not reset or delete active work.
3. **Enforced resource contracts:** Planned gates and actual commands declare private paths, shared resources, scope/capacity, execution profile and release conditions. All production build/test launch paths used by workers/checkers go through enforcement; prose instructions alone are insufficient. Undeclared/unproven effects conservatively queue for an appropriate exclusive profile. Unsupported enforcement cannot silently run unprotected or count as accepted evidence. A private fixture/test registry does not authorize unrelated production effects.
4. **Steam and GPU safety:** Default Steam exclusivity covers the whole experiment and rollback, and conflicts with relevant GPU/cache/stress work. Queue a second Steam request while isolated CPU work can progress within reservations. Verify actual Steam binary/environment/driver/cache identity and preserved originals. Detect outside-session changes, prevent unsafe restoration over a newer installation, and quarantine incomplete cleanup. Never terminate a user's unrelated session or wipe normal caches to acquire a slot. Fake fixtures must cover these rules; real integration is a separately authorized, explicitly reported gate if the implementation claims that support.
5. **Unattended lifecycle:** Persist fair waiting, automatic admission/resumption, cancellation, owner restart/crash recovery and resource quarantine/recovery. Ordinary contention needs no user action. Reclaim only after ownership/descendants/restoration are reconciled. An irreconcilable external change may produce a precise exceptional decision; it must not turn contention into a routine manual workflow. Define queue-versus-execution deadlines without reducing test rigor, adding silent repair attempts or fabricating completion.
6. **No quality regression:** Preserve fresh planner/implementer/unit checker/separate final checker, original acceptance and test mappings, required gate execution, bounded repair, issue/base/candidate revalidation, honest failed/unsupported/incomplete states, issue evidence and one verified PR per satisfied run. Never skip tests, relax assertions, enlarge test timeouts to mask contention, accept contaminated measurements, reuse another candidate's test report or auto-merge without existing authorization. Pin helper/tool identities so a concurrent harness self-update cannot silently change another run's protocol.
7. **Documentation and operational contract:** Update the tracked skill, state/role guidance and verification guide with run selection, resource inventory, supported OS/filesystems/host boundaries, queue status/recovery and migration. Explicitly state the enforcement boundary and residual effects of outside processes. Preserve https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/39 delivery/wrap-up guarantees when both features coexist.

## Required automated verification

Use assertion-bearing tests with independent processes, barriers/events and bounded watchdogs; sleeps alone are not a race oracle. Include a serial reference execution and compare semantic outputs/outcomes. Existing harness regressions remain required.

- Two runs in linked worktrees and two clones against a disposable bare remote; interleaved initialize/report/checkpoint/publish/complete; no state/report/approval crossover or dropped history. Simultaneous same-issue/root-child claims yield exactly one owner. Completing A leaves B active and resumable.
- Simultaneous artifact publications, stale CAS, changed remote endpoints, remote advancement, transient outage, response loss before/after every mutation, terminal checkpoint publication failure and restart. No force push, duplicate issue/PR/comment or unsafe history adoption. Genuine conflicting owners are fenced.
- Two independent test processes/CTest invocations claiming the same mock Steam/GPU/cache resource cannot overlap; distinct proven-private CPU fixtures do overlap. Different clones on one host use the same host-resource key. Different simulated hosts do not unnecessarily share local-resource reservations but still coordinate remote/task claims. Alias/symlink and multi-resource/hierarchical conflicts are covered.
- A fake Steam installation/session/cache test asserts full-transaction exclusivity, controlled baseline/cold/warm identity, rollback verification, no cache contamination, preserved user files and no unsafe restore after external modification. Do not require logging into Steam to run the default regression suite.
- Coordinator/runner death, SIGTERM/SIGKILL, lost heartbeat, PID reuse, lock-FD inheritance, daemonized grandchildren, delegated service activity, reboot/restart and suspended old owner resumption. Never release ownership to the next test while stale work can still act. Cleanup failures quarantine the resource while unrelated eligible runs continue.
- Queue persists through restart; contention auto-resumes without prompts; fairness, cancellation, long waits, budget accounting and deadlock avoidance are asserted. Fake clocks exercise deadline behavior without extending execution allowance. Separate process evidence proves an admitted test owns the reservation before it launches.
- Undeclared effects and unavailable isolation backends cannot fall through to unsafe execution. Host pressure/quiet-window conflicts do not silently weaken test outcomes. Platform implementations get native tests; unavailable native/real Steam/GPU verification remains explicitly incomplete or outside a narrowly stated claim, never inferred from Linux mocks.
- Assert the existing independent-verification/publication fences under concurrent load and migration. All acceptance evidence remains bound to its own issue/input/base/candidate/plan/attempt and resource environment.

## Research evidence and limits

On 28 October 2026, a standard-library Python probe in a disposable repository (45-second external watchdog, per-command deadlines) asserted: two separate clones both acquired their own local `harness-run.lock`; a common resource lock excluded a second owner; from a shared artifact ancestor the first non-force push succeeded and a competing divergent push was rejected. This verifies those local Git/flock mechanisms, not production parallel harness support or a live multi-host deployment.

Inspected the current helper, role contracts, existing concurrency/artifact tests, CTest registration, fixed-name tests, Linux/Windows external-replayer IPC naming and Steam verification procedures. No production source, active-run state, Steam installation, game or GPU workload was changed for research. CMake/CTest were not on PATH, so cross-CTest exclusion is a design inference/required future test, not an executed result. The Steam runtime tools GitLab page was access-blocked; no claim depends on its contents. Web sources were read on 28 October 2026; implementation must verify supported installed versions.

## Scope and relationships

One implementation request under https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/9, covering run coordination plus the resource enforcement needed to claim safe concurrency. Related: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/39 (delivery/wrap-up), https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/36 (artifact guarantees), https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/37 (issue identity), and the motivating https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/10. No new blocked-by dependency on #39 is asserted merely because the code overlaps; coordinate the integration order against actual delivery state. Do not close the harness parent while other required children remain incomplete.

Filing this issue does not implement concurrency, bypass today's single-run restriction, start another harness run or authorize live Steam experiments. If split during planning, create native sub-issues with full acceptance coverage and real prerequisite mappings.

observation.title: Allow unattended parallel harness runs with isolated state and shared-resource scheduling
